The existence clause of Question 36 has an affirmative answer. Take the coordinatewise ring $R=\bigoplus_{p\text{ prime}}\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and let $E=R$ as an additive submonoid. Given $r,a\in R$, the Chinese remainder theorem on the finite support of $a$ gives a natural number $n$ with $ra=na=ar$. Every finite sum of products having the other factor in $M$ therefore lies in $M$, for every additive submonoid $M$. The coordinate indicator of the support of $a$ multiplies $a$ to itself, so $EM=M=ME$. A singleton at a prime outside the support of any proposed ring identity contradicts the identity equation. Lean independently checks the exact parameterized optimum. For every finite field of odd order q ≥ 7 with the two stated parity and nonsquare conditions, the greatest class count at n = q(q + 1) + 2 is n − 1. The lower bound takes all weight-(q − 1) subsets of each projective line and adds one unused coordinate. Attainment of n would force a two-point group design. Its square integer incidence matrix would have Gram determinant (q + 1)^(m + 2)(q − 1)^(m − 1), whose prime multiplicities contradict it being a square.
